summary: A questionnaire from David Crocker for collecting information about graphics resources at each ARPANET site. The answers were to be compiled into an ARPANET Graphics Resources Notebook. It asks about local graphics experts, hardware, capabilities and differences when used over the network.

plainLanguage.summary: A form asking each school what drawing tools and screens it has, so a big list can be made and people know who has what.

subtitle: Questionnaire to survey graphics hardware and capabilities at ARPANET sites.

tldr.problem: ARPANET sites have different graphics hardware and capabilities, and nobody has a comprehensive list of what is available where for remote access.
tldr.mechanism: David Crocker circulates a detailed questionnaire asking each site to describe its graphics experts, hardware, capabilities, network access procedures, and any limitations when used remotely.
tldr.outcome: Responses will be compiled into an ARPANET Graphics Resources Notebook so sites know where to find graphics services on the network.

today: RFC 351 is a June 1972 survey questionnaire from UCLA for the Network Graphics Working Group. It is marked Unknown status. This RFC documents the early graphics community's effort to catalog network resources in the pre-web era.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 351 is a questionnaire from David Crocker (UCLA) created for the Network Graphics Working Group. The goal is to survey graphics resources across the ARPANET so that sites can discover what graphics hardware and services are available on the network.

As the ARPANET grows and more sites add graphics capabilities, a central inventory helps users and administrators understand the landscape and plan access to remote graphics systems.
sections.plainLanguage: A person is asking each school to say what drawing computers and tools they have. This will be collected into one big list so everyone knows who can help with graphics work.

sections.title: Survey Questions
sections.content:
The questionnaire asks sites to provide:

  • Organization name and host number(s)
  • Local graphics experts (names and phone)
  • Graphics hardware installed
  • Local graphics capabilities and software
  • Differences in abilities over the network
  • Default settings when entering remotely
  • Graphics routines available remotely
  • Login procedures and process-initiation steps for network access
  • Attention/escape signals used
  • Demo account details and programs available
  • Additional interests and capabilities
sections.plainLanguage: The form asks: who works there, what hardware do you have, what programs run, how do you log in from the network, who can show it off, and anything special.

sections.title: Submission and Compilation
sections.content: Sites should complete the form and return it to David Crocker, preferably as a NIC Journal entry (for easy data processing). His mailing address is given at UCLA, c/o Jon Postel in the Computer Science Department. The responses will be compiled into the ARPANET Graphics Resources Notebook, which will document where graphics services can be found across the network.
sections.plainLanguage: Mail back your answers to the person listed, preferably in a computer format. All the answers will be put into a book listing everyone's graphics tools.
